sections.title: VRV CU / FCU Test Results
sections._note:
Scope is `location`, not `equipment`: one sheet covers every condensing and fan coil unit serving a room — the source lists a CU and its FCU together under "AMK3 Level 2 Network Room" — so the record belongs to the room, with each unit a row.

Six rows to match the printed grid; the source ships two filled and four blank. Nothing is prefilled: the units on the source sheet are one project's data, not template wording (SPEC §5.1).

Landscape like the source. Measured with all six rows filled: the grid is 268.8mm inside 269mm of printable width — an exact fit — and 143.7mm of a 158mm body, leaving room for about one more row before it spills. The sign-off is the top-level `footer` and takes the page PrintView gives it; in the flow it measured 82.1mm and put the page 82.4mm over.

`font_size` is declared for the on-screen form only — print-section.tsx does not read it, so the printed grid is print.css's 10pt whatever this says.

columns.label: CU Low
columns._note: Text, not number: an FCU row has no CU pressure and the source is filled "-".

columns.label: Current L1
columns._note: The source packs one cell with either a single figure (single-phase FCU) or three stacked lines L1= / L2= / L3= (three-phase CU). Split into three columns: a flat table renders one control per cell, and three separate readings are three values regardless. A single-phase unit fills L1 only, which is also how it reads back out.

columns.label: Rated Power
columns._note: Number with a kW unit; the source is typed "3.23kw" with the unit inline, which the unit column now carries.

columns.label: Remarks
columns._note: `text`, matching the source's single-line remarks input. (It was tried as a `textarea` on the theory that it drove row height; measured, it made no difference — row height comes from the cell padding, not the control.)
